blockNote: Debug Man - an unused developer NPC that maxes the player's stats and offers a warp menu with 21 destinations (Bank 0B, 781856-782712). No scene script, scene_actors record or spawn call in extracted/ references it, so it never appears in the retail game.
=== STRUCTURE ===

The actor-def (sprite index 2, flags 0, header byte $10) entry runs once: MarkSolidHere, SetInteractHandler(DebugManInteract), SetEntryHere, RTL. Nothing runs per frame afterwards; talking to the NPC starts DebugManInteract.

DebugManInteract writes max HP and HP = 40, STR and DEF = 127 (16-bit stores, so the high bytes become 0) and abilityBitmask = $FF (all abilities), prints the greeting and opens the first menu. It does this on every conversation, so talking to Debug Man again resets the stats to those values.
=== MENU CHAIN ===

The menu is 7 levels. Each level is PrintDialogString (one page of 4 rows) followed by COP DialogueOptions( #04, #00, table ): the two operand bytes form the menu-layout word handed to MenuSelectionHandler, which returns 0 for B (cancel) or the confirmed row + 1. DialogueOptions uses that as the index into the word table and resumes the script there. Every table therefore has 5 entries: [0] = DebugManQuit (B), [1] to [4] = rows 1 to 4.
Row 1 of levels 1 to 6 is 'Others' and opens the next level; rows 2 to 4 are destinations. Level 7 has 'Quit' as row 1 (table entries 0 and 1 are both DebugManQuit) and three destinations.

A destination leaf prints 'Ok! See you again!', queues the scene change with COP QueueMapChange( scene, X px, Y px, facing, scroll params ) and returns with RTL. The facing byte is an index into direction_velocity_table (it selects the first sprite frame of the spawned player). The leaves change no stats and no flags.
=== DESTINATIONS (scene id, then the leaf label) ===

Level 1: Great Wall $82 (code_0BEED5), LAST GAIA LOOK = the ending sequence $E5 (code_0BEEF3), EDOWA-DO = Edward Castle $0A (code_0BEEE4). The ROM order of the last two leaves is the reverse of the row order; the table maps row 3 to the $E5 leaf and row 4 to the $0A leaf.

Level 2: Itory Village $15, Moon Tribe camp $1A, underground castle $0F. Level 3: Euro $91, Natives' Village $AC, Dao $C3. Level 4: Inca Ruins $1C, Freejia $32 (HANANOMIYAKO), Diamond Mine $3E (DAIYAMONDO).
Level 5: Sky Garden $4C, Seaside Palace $5A, Mu $5F. Level 6: Angel Village $69, a second entry point of Natives' Village $AC and of Dao $C3. Level 7: Pyramid $CC, Watermia $78, Angkor Wat $B0.
That is 21 leaves; the old header said about 35 destinations, and the old labels for $32 (Gold Ship) and $3E (Diamond Coast) and the swapped $0A / $E5 comments were wrong.

blockNote: Enemy drop spawner for gems and heals (Bank 00, 57129-57340). The names say 'dark gem', but what drops is a pickup carrying item id $83 to $86 of GiveItemToPlayer: 1, 2 or 5 gems, or a 5 HP heal.
=== CALLER ===

StandardEnemyDefeatHandler reaches EnemyGemDropRouter when the defeated enemy's stat byte +3 (enemy-stats gemDropType) is nonzero and scene flag $0300 is clear. The router spawns one of three entries with SpawnListAppend (flags $0420, so the pickup inherits the dead enemy's position through CopyActorState): value 1 = SpawnDarkGemType1 (fixed $83), value 2 = DarkGemDropAnimVariantB (fixed $84), any other nonzero value (3) = DarkGemDropTierPicker (random, see below).
=== THE PICKUP ===

The actor carries its item id in chatPtr ($7F000A,X) and has the 'friendly' flag $0020 in its $10 (from the spawn flags). When the player overlaps it, combat_collision.InteractionDamage_NPCChat calls GiveItemToPlayer(chatPtr) and turns the actor into NpcDespawnStub. Ids: $83 = 1 gem, $84 = 2 gems, $85 = 5 gems (cap 999), $86 = hpToHeal += 5 (UpdateHUD refills 1 HP every 8 frames) plus the spark effect and SFX $22.

Each entry also spawns a marked child, interaction_handlers.collect_handler_gem (flags $2700), which pulls the pickup toward the player while L / R is held. The pickup is the marked parent ($12 bit $0040 set by SpawnAfterMarked), so its Die also removes the child. Each body clears $10 bit $0400 that the $0420 spawn flags set (see OQ-I049-3).
=== LIFETIME (spriteset_enemies animation lists) ===

Gems: anim 4 / 5 / 6 (gems $83 / $84 / $85) for 10 passes (about 75 ticks each: a 60-tick still frame and 5 shimmer frames of 3 ticks, about 750 ticks), then the blink anim 9 / $0A / $0B for 150 passes (2 ticks each, about 300 ticks), then Die. Heal: anim $22 for 180 passes (2 ticks, about 360 ticks), then anim $35 for 60 passes (4 ticks, about 240 ticks), then Die.
=== WEIGHTED DROP (DarkGemDropTierPicker) ===

HP tier by the player's HP against max HP: HP <= max/4 uses table group $20, HP <= max/2 uses group $10, otherwise group 0. A random byte is compared against the group's four ascending thresholds (the last is $0100, so it always matches) and the first row whose threshold is above the byte gives the body to run. Probabilities of 256 outcomes:

HP above half: $86 heal 5.9%, $85 5 gems 17.6%, $84 2 gems 36.3%, $83 1 gem 40.2%. HP between a quarter and a half: $85 9.8%, $83 19.9%, $86 30.1%, $84 40.2%. HP at or below a quarter: $84 4.7%, $83 15.2%, $85 29.7%, $86 50.4%. The heal becomes the likeliest drop when the player is low on HP.

blockNote: Per-frame camera tracking actor (Bank 00, 60144-60314), the camera actor of 220+ field scenes. It reads the player's position, derives the scroll position that centres the player (clamped to the scene's window) and publishes the distance from the current scroll to that target as effectDeltaX / effectDeltaY for the visual_effect_pipeline actors (effect_velocity_init, effect_position_update, effect_subpixel_math). It scrolls nothing itself.
=== ENTRY AND FREEZE ===

actor-def: sprite 0, flags 0, header byte $2C. Every run sets $12 bit $1000 (the display / overlay-active qualifier that lets the actor run in the display-filtered and overlay-only modes; CopyActorState never copies it), calls SetEntryHere and returns at once when layerPriorityFlag bit $0200 is set (camera frozen; the attack setup in player_character sets it).
=== PLAYER POSITION ===

D := playerActorDp (the player's actor slot), so $14 / $16 are the player's pixel X / Y. playerXPos := X - 8 and playerYPos := Y - $10 (sprite-adjusted reference point), playerXTile / playerYTile := those values >> 4. These four words are refreshed every frame, also while the target is held.
=== TARGET (skipped while playerFlags bit $0100, forced walk, is set) ===

Per axis, with P = the player actor's pixel position (not the adjusted one): t = P - $80. If t is negative or below cameraOffset, the target is cameraOffset (left / top limit). Otherwise e = t + $100; if e is at or beyond cameraBounds the target is cameraBounds - $100, else it is t. So cameraOffset is the left / top edge of the scene's window and cameraBounds the right / bottom edge. There is no dead zone: the old note called the P - 128 centring a 'dead zone'.

Both axes use the constants $80 and $100. Horizontally that centres the player in the 256-pixel view; vertically the target puts the player 128 lines below the top of a 224-line screen, 16 lines below the middle (OQ-I049-4). The result goes to cameraTargetX / cameraTargetY.
=== DELTAS ===

effectDeltaX := cameraTargetX - bg1ScrollH and effectDeltaY := cameraTargetY - mapScrollV ($068E, the vertical scroll that UploadScrollRegisters writes to BG1VOFS; the old comment said BG2). This also runs while the forced walk holds the target, so the deltas keep following whatever forced_walk wrote to the target.
=== DEAD CODE ===
loc_00EB48 and loc_00EB74 (LDA cameraBoundsX / cameraBoundsY, BRA) are never branched to: the preceding code ends in BRA, and no other file references them.
